subject.title: iOS remote pairing UX: QR crash, onboarding paste fails, Settings paste works (cellular); feedback on edge auth + mobile wss://

question: Should OpenClaw document a supported split-host public exposure pattern where browser/operator traffic stays behind an identity-aware proxy and mobile `wss://` pairing uses a separate OpenClaw-token/device-bootstrap hostname?
rationale: The remaining ask affects public Gateway exposure, trusted-proxy auth, and mobile setup-code bootstrap semantics, so automation should not define the supported security posture.

options.title: Document Split-Host Mobile Pairing
options.body: Add a security-reviewed advanced recipe covering separate admin/mobile hostnames, no HTTP SSO redirect on the mobile pairing host, strict `trustedProxies`, token auth, and Settings paste/QR expectations.

options.title: Keep Tailscale Serve As The Only First-Class Remote Path
options.body: Leave public `wss://` mobile pairing as operator-managed advanced setup and document only the Tailscale Serve default plus existing generic reverse-proxy warnings.

options.title: Defer Public Mobile Pairing Direction
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers decide whether public mobile pairing beyond Tailscale Serve should become a supported deployment shape.

recommendation.title: Document Split-Host Mobile Pairing
recommendation.body: Add a security-reviewed advanced recipe covering separate admin/mobile hostnames, no HTTP SSO redirect on the mobile pairing host, strict `trustedProxies`, token auth, and Settings paste/QR expectations.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the route-list fix, merged the QR repair, and is the strongest available owner signal for the mobile pairing/security-doc boundary.
